Daily Brief

European Union leaders concluded a tense 12-hour summit in Brussels without agreement on the bloc's 2028-2034 budget, with negotiations set to resume in December amid deep divisions over spending priorities and Ukraine aid [BBC], [RFI]. The impasse comes as Ukraine braces for another difficult winter, with President Zelensky sharply criticizing President Trump's characterization of Vladimir Putin as 'my friend,' comparing it to befriending Hitler during World War Two [BBC]. In Spain, voters head to the polls Sunday in an election dominated by housing affordability protests, with polls suggesting the conservative People's Party will form a government with far-right Vox—potentially the first time the far right enters national government since Franco's dictatorship [BBC]. A significant cybersecurity breach at the U.S. Air Force's Cloud One platform has compromised systems managing sensitive tactical, personnel, and logistics data across hundreds of locations worldwide [The Hindu]. Meanwhile, the UN's food agencies warned that hunger will worsen in 16 countries over the next six months, with Sudan, Yemen, South Sudan, Somalia, and northern Nigeria facing the gravest risks as conflict, fuel costs, and aid cuts converge [Globe and Mail].

01 Economics

EU Budget Talks Collapse as Member States Clash Over Spending and Ukraine Aid

  • EU leaders ended 12 hours of negotiations in Brussels without agreement on the 2028-2034 budget, with talks postponed until December 17-18
  • A group of net-contributor countries including Germany, Netherlands, Austria, and Sweden opposed higher spending proposals favored by France and Italy
  • Germany's Chancellor Merz insisted that Ukraine aid of €45 billion must have unanimous EU support, while Slovakia, Czech Republic, and Hungary objected to the loan
  • European Council President Antonio Costa's proposal to cut €204 billion from the budget and introduce a digital tax failed to bridge divisions

Spain Heads to Polls Sunday with Far-Right Poised to Enter Government

  • Spanish voters go to ballot boxes Sunday with polls showing Socialist PM Pedro Sánchez likely to lose power after eight years
  • Conservative People's Party (PP) is projected to win and form a government with far-right Vox party
  • If Vox enters government, it would be the first time the far right holds national power in Spain's 50 years of post-Franco democracy
  • Housing affordability has dominated the campaign, with protesters jangling house keys across the country; PP leader pledged to build one million new homes

04 Technology

Hackers Breach U.S. Air Force Cloud One Computing Platform

  • Hackers breached the U.S. Air Force's flagship Cloud One cloud computing platform, discovered during system upgrades within the past month
  • Cloud One manages sensitive applications including air defense radar data, personnel records, pay systems, and munitions tracking across 200+ locations worldwide
  • The platform combines resources from Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle, and Alphabet; SAIC was the prime contractor
  • The Air Force declined to comment on specifics; the identity of hackers and scope of data theft remain unknown

05 Society

UN Warns Hunger Crisis to Worsen in 16 Countries as Conflicts and Aid Cuts Collide

  • UN food agencies report hunger will worsen in 16 countries over the next six months, with Sudan, Yemen, South Sudan, Somalia, and northern Nigeria at highest risk
  • In Sudan, nearly 19.5 million people (41% of population) face crisis-level hunger; famine risk persists in 13 areas through January
  • Sorghum and diesel prices in Sudan have more than doubled due to fighting and Middle East-linked fuel cost increases
  • Gaza was downgraded one level following the October 2025 ceasefire, though 67% of the population still faces crisis-level hunger or worse
